subject: Audit export schema, redaction controls & deletion-proof requirements
messages:

Cc: Tom Ellison <tom.ellison@odinbank.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Export redaction + schema questions (RFP section 5)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we pull together answers for Section 5 of our RFP (Logging & Auditability), we have a couple of interlocking asks that we need answered for our security and privacy teams:

1) When we request a bulk audit export, can Redwood produce a manifest that includes a cryptographic signature (HMAC) and a stable event schema so we can verify completeness and integrity?
2) For exported events containing PII, what redaction/pseudonymization options do you offer at export time vs. at rest? We need to know if you can run deterministic pseudonyms (consistent across exports) and whether we can request reversible tokens for incident re‑linking under legal controls.
3) For legal hold and deletion proof, can Redwood provide verifiable proof that records beyond our retention policy have been purged (e.g., tombstone manifests, signed deletion logs)?

Attached is a short worksheet from our legal team (ODN-RFP worksheet). Can you respond with technical detail and any sample manifests or schema docs?

Appreciate it—Priyanka
Security & Privacy
Odin Bank

Subject: Re: Export redaction + schema questions (RFP section 5)

Hi Priyanka—thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vivek (our engineering lead on exportability) and Ben (your account lead) so we can give concrete artifacts.

Quick summary of what we can deliver today and where we suggest clarifying scoping in the RFP:
- Signed export manifest: we include a signed JSON manifest for each export. The manifest contains export_id, account_id, time_range, file checksums (SHA-256), and an HMAC using a customer-specific key that we exchange over the account onboarding KMS.
- Stable export schema: events are delivered as NDJSON with a published, versioned schema. We'll share the schema and a CSV mapping of Redwood event fields to typical regulatory fields.
- Redaction/pseudonymization: two primary modes available:
  * Online redaction (export-time): you can request field-level redaction rules (mask, truncate, hash). Deterministic hashing (HMAC-SHA256 with account salt) is supported for pseudonymization; reversible tokens are available through our Token Vault under an approved legal process.
  * At-rest controls: we maintain encryption and configurable retention windows per account; exports do not modify data at rest unless you request an export-then-delete workflow.
- Deletion proofs: we support signed deletion logs and tombstone manifests for retention-driven purges. For higher-assurance requests we can produce an immutable snapshot signed by Redwood (timestamped, manifest + proof-of-deletion entries).

I'm attaching a quick export-schema mapping CSV and a short playbook that outlines redaction options and the legal workflow for reversible tokens. Vivek will follow up with technical detail on manifests and delivery mechanics (S3 vs. secure transfer).

Next steps: Vivek to add the engineering specifics by EOD. Ben, can we schedule a 30-min run-through for Thursday to review the artifacts with Priyanka's team?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Export redaction + schema questions (RFP section 5)

Hi Priyanka — diving into the technical answers you asked for. TL;DR: all of these are supported; below are formats and example artifacts.

1) Export manifest and integrity
- Format: JSON manifest (manifest_v2) containing: export_id, account_id, start_ts, end_ts, file_list [ {filename, sha256, size_bytes} ], schema_version, export_tool_version, delivered_via (S3/GCS/FTPS).
- Signature: manifest has two signatures: an HMAC (customer-specific secret derived from onboarding KMS) and a Redwood ECDSA signature for non-repudiation. Example manifest snippet is available in the shared Drive link.

2) Stable schema and NDJSON packaging
- Events exported as NDJSON, one JSON object per event. Each event includes a header block: {redwood_event_id, created_at, actor_id (pseudonymized if requested), event_type, payload, provenance: {node_id, model_version}}.
- We publish a schema registry (semantic versioning). When you request an export we include schema_version in the manifest so you can validate incoming payloads.

3) Redaction/pseudonymization approaches
- Deterministic pseudonymization: field hashing using account-specific HMAC salt. This is consistent across exports and reversible only if you use the Token Vault reversible token workflow.
- Export-time redaction rules: deterministic-hash, mask (X…X), truncate, or remove-field. Rules can be applied per-field and scoped to time-range on the export request.
- Token Vault: reversible tokens are kept encrypted under a customer-managed KMS key and require explicit authorized calls (audit trail + legal signoff) to re-link. We record a re-link event into an immutable audit ledger.

4) Deletion / purge proofing
- Retention policy enforcement: accounts define retention policies (e.g., 7y for audit_event); when objects are purged we emit a signed tombstone entry containing: event_id_range, purge_ts, purge_reason, checksum_of_deleted_files.
- Proof artifacts: tombstone manifests, signed deletion logs, and an optional immutable snapshot (WORM) of the manifest signed with Redwood ECDSA and timestamped via our timestamping service.
- For legal matters, we can provide chain-of-custody packaging: manifest + file checksums + delivery receipts (S3 access logs / signed FTPS transfer receipts).

5) Delivery mechanics and formats
- Primary delivery options: S3 (roles with restricted bucket), pre-signed URL, FTPS, or Redwood-managed encrypted transfer. Files are zipped with a top-level manifest. We support incremental exports (change-only deltas) or full-range exports.

Sample limitations/notes:
- Deterministic pseudonyms are stable only per-account salt. If you change salt or request cross-account joins, you'll need a reconciliation plan.
- Reversible token workflow requires a documented legal process (we log every re-link attempt in an immutable audit table).

I'll attach a small example manifest and an example NDJSON event sample to the Drive link for your team to validate.

- Vivek

Hi Marissa / Vivek—thanks for the rapid detail. A couple of follow-ups from our engineering team: 

1) For the HMAC on the manifest, can you confirm the key lifecycle? We need automated key rotation without breaking deterministic pseudonyms in historic exports.
2) For reversible tokens in Token Vault: what is the SLA for a re-link request (audit + legal signoff path) and can the process be integrated with our ticketing system so we maintain our internal change log?
3) For deletion proofs: we need a canonical format that includes a signed timestamp + a pointer to the exact S3 objects deleted. Can Redwood include the S3 object keys and a signed purge manifest per purge job?

Attached: our filled RFP worksheet with examples marked. Can you answer inline where possible?

Subject: Re: Export redaction + schema questions (RFP section 5)

Tom/Priyanka—good questions. Short answers and proposed next steps: 

- HMAC lifecycle: keys are rotated quarterly by default. Deterministic pseudonym salt is separate from manifest HMAC key; rotation of HMAC does not affect pseudonym stability. If you want salt rotation policies we can set a migration path (we keep historical salt versions for backwards re-linking if requested under Token Vault governance).
- Re-link SLA & integration: standard re-link SLA is 48 business hours after receipt of all required legal artifacts; we can automate the intake via a webhook to your ticketing system and include the ticket ID in our immutable re-link audit entry.
- Signed purge manifests: yes, we will include S3 object keys, timestamps, sizes, and a signed tombstone manifest for each purge job. Those are also exportable as a compressed artifact with its own manifest and signature.

Action items:
1) Ben to schedule a 30-minute artifacts review for Thu 2027-04-29 11:00 PT.
2) Vivek to upload the sample manifest + NDJSON example to the shared Drive and drop an example HMAC verification snippet.
3) Monica to coordinate a scoped POA with Odin for reversible-token governance and legal intake.

Ben / Monica — please own the scheduling and intake so we can respond in-line in the RFP. Priyanka / Tom — thanks again; we'll turn the Drive items into the RFP answers and mark the sections as "provided" in the worksheet.

Best,
